drug_class: Topical anticancer agent (dual-mechanism microtubule and Src kinase inhibitor)
purpose: Tirbanibulin is a prescription cream used to treat actinic keratosis, which are rough, scaly patches on the skin caused by years of sun exposure. These patches are considered precancerous, meaning they could turn into skin cancer if left untreated. Using this cream helps get rid of those patches and lowers the risk of them becoming something more serious.
how_it_works: This cream works in two ways to stop abnormal skin cells from growing and spreading. It interferes with the tiny structures inside cells that help them divide and multiply. It also blocks a specific protein that tells abnormal cells to keep growing, so those cells eventually die off and healthier skin can replace them.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects happen right where you apply the cream and include redness, flaking or peeling skin, scaling, and a feeling of irritation or discomfort on the treated area. Some people may also notice swelling or a slight burning sensation. These effects are usually mild and go away after you finish the treatment.
warnings: This cream is only meant to be used on the skin — never put it in your eyes, mouth, or nose, and keep it away from those areas. Wash your hands thoroughly after applying it. Avoid using it on open wounds or irritated skin. Tell your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, as the safety in these situations has not been fully established. Do not use more than directed, as overuse can increase irritation without improving results.
typical_dosing: You apply a thin layer of the cream once daily to the affected area on your face or scalp for five days in a row, then stop. Your doctor will guide you on exactly how much to use and which area to treat. One full treatment course is just those five days, and your skin will continue to heal after you finish applying it.
